title: Cell spotter
prompt: Find the scale where a single cell fills your screen.
hint: Cells are about 30 micrometres across, which is 3 × 10⁻⁵ metres. Try the ruler near the 10⁻⁵ mark, then hold still.

title: Ten powers smaller
prompt: Zoom to something 10¹⁰ times smaller than you.
hint: Watch the badge under the view height: it says how many powers of ten smaller than you the view is. Atoms live around here.

title: Orbit keeper
prompt: Zoom out until the whole Solar System fills your view.
hint: Neptune's orbit is about 9 billion kilometres across, which is 9 × 10¹² metres.

title: Edge of knowledge
prompt: Dive down to the Planck length, the smallest scale scientists talk about.
hint: Keep zooming in past the proton. Most of the way there is empty. You are looking for 10⁻³⁵ metres.

title: Sun sizer
prompt: How many Earths fit across the Sun?
hint: Open the Compare tray and pick Earth and the Sun. It shows both at true scale and says the ratio in words.

title: Hair's breadth
prompt: How many red blood cells would fit side by side across the width of a human hair?
hint: A red blood cell is about 7 micrometres across. A hair is about 70 micrometres wide. Check with the Compare tray.

title: Giant star
prompt: Estimate how many Suns would fit across the red supergiant Betelgeuse.
hint: Betelgeuse is about 10¹² metres across and the Sun is about 10⁹ metres. Divide, or let the Compare tray do it.

title: Mountain maths
prompt: Estimate how many people, standing on each other's heads, would reach the height of Mount Everest.
hint: Mount Everest is about 8,849 metres high and a person is about 1.7 metres tall.
